There are likely at least 4 or 5 core FPS gameplay styles that have large markets. Cover based (gears of war), non-cover realistic (CS), run and gun (DOOM) and likely another or two that have really big markets but haven't been well designed yet. Then some smaller markets that have been only lightly tapped like Puzzle FPS games (Portal and Superhot), Stealth (Thief) and mass destruction games (Red Faction), I'm not sure these styles are as strong a market as those above.

So a company like Valve could make 3 or 4 FPS games without much player base shared between them. Counterstrike is more realistic and highly competitive, Team Fortress 2 is cartoonish and more of a run and gun party game, Portal is a puzzle game, Left 4 Dead is less realistic counterstrike (when CS:GO came out I bet most L4D2 players switched games), Half Life is a single player Puzzle/run and gun game. So the player bases of these games are actually reasonably different (except L4D and CS). Players might play multiple of them, but they play them for different reasons.

I'm not being exhaustive, this is just a thought exercise. I know there are other Popular FPS games that don't really fall into these categories perfectly. This just is to point out the niche markets within FPS games and that major companies have been chasing success in the saturated markets and ignoring the almost empty ones.
